newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 3.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Feb 3.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

MIM Holdings Ltd chief executive Nick Stump said late on Friday the Australia-based resources company should emerge from the current half year in better shape. Earlier MIM announced a half year net loss of A$12 million, down from a A$58.9 million profit a year earlier. MIM's half year net loss before abnormals and exchange losses was A$8.8 million, down from last year's profit of A$23.6 million, but better than market expectations of a A$10 million to A$20 million loss. Stump is due to give another press briefing later on Monday.
CSR Ltd said on Friday it had engaged investment bankers Credit Suisse First Boston to assist in evaluating options for the restructure of the group's timber operations.

North Ltd said late on Friday it was keen to proceed to a full feasibility study on a new iron ore project in the Australia's northwest, estimating the deposit would cost up to A$1 billion to develop.
Lend Lease Corp Ltd said on Friday it would start an onmarket share buy-back scheme for 0.969 percent of its shares.
* Mt Edon Gold Mines NL A$2.12 (+0.01)
Mt Edon posted a A$5.23 million net profit for the half year late on Friday, compared with a A$4.90 million loss in the previous comparable half.

Shell Australia Ltd confirmed on Friday that a joint-venture exploration team including Cultus had made an oil and gas find in the Browse Basin offshore northwest Australia. It said the discovery could be comparable in size to other recent discoveries in the Greater North West Shelf.
Equatorial Mining NL on Friday recommended shareholders reject the increased takeover offer of 30 cents a share by Quay Mining Pty Ltd, wholly-owned by Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) Society.

The Australian Financial Review reported on Monday that the people of Guadalcanal were due to hold a mass public rally later today to consider blockading Ross Mining's A$69 million Gold Ridge project.
